chunks.heading: **<u>MECHANISM FOR FRAMING, CONSULTATION AND ISSUANCE OF REGULATIONS</u>**
chunks.content:
In order to ensure an expedite regulation making process in line with the Non Legislative Recommendations of the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission, the regulation framing procedure is rationalized as under: 

Step 1: To seek the approval from the Authority for drafting and publishing the draft regulations for stakeholder consultation. In cases deemed necessary, the approval of the Authority may be obtained by circulation. 

Step 2: Preparation of draft regulations 

Step 3: The draft regulations shall be circulated to Chairman, Whole Time Members and all HoDs and necessary discussions shall be carried out. 

Step 4: Publishing the exposure draft of the regulations, seeking public comments as well as comments of the employees of the Authority.  A time period of 21 days may be granted to the stakeholders to respond. 

Step 5: Examination of comments received from the stakeholders, public and employees of the Authority (within 10 days time). Comments received to be listed out along with the remarks of the department. 

Step 6: Placing the draft regulations before the Insurance Advisory Committee in accordance with Section 26 of IRDA Act, 1999. 

Step 7: Preparation of final draft regulations after considering the suggestions received from IAC (Five days time). 

Step 8: Vetting of draft regulations by Legal department, IRDAI. 

Step 9: Placing the final regulations along with the comments received and the remarks of the department, before the Authority for approval. 

Step 10: Notification and publication of regulations within two weeks of the approval by the Authority. 

The nodal departments shall comply with the timelines prescribed above while framing of new Regulations and amendments to existing Regulations.

chunks.heading: **<u>MECHANISM FOR FRAMING EMERGENCY REGULATIONS</u>**
chunks.content:
Emergency Regulation making: 

**(1)** The following requirements must be complied with for framing regulations in an emergency where the entire internal and external consultation procedure cannot be complied with: 

(a) A background note of the regulations indicating the following: 

      - The relevant sections of the Act exercising powers under which the regulation is issued 

      - The brief description of the content of the Regulations 

         - In case of fresh regulations 

            - The purpose which is intended to be achieved through the regulations 

            - Previous circulars / instructions / guidelines in the matter, if any and consolidation thereof in the present regulation. 

         - In case of amending regulations 

            - The provisions intended to be amended 

            - Key changes made 

            - Rationale for changes made 

   - (b) The emergency for resorting to framing regulations in a manner different from usual process. 

   - (c) Draft Regulations in the exact format in which it is supposed to be notified. 

   - (d) The draft may be circulated to the Chairman, Members and senior officers of the IRDAI. 

   - (e) The draft may be circulated to IAC members requesting their comments within two working days. 

   - (f) Vetting of the Regulations by Legal Department. 

   - (g) Notification of the regulations as soon as possible. 

   - (h) Press Release giving the background 

- **(2)** Emergency regulations cease to have effect after one hundred and eighty days from the date on which the regulation is notified.
